subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which context-overflow facts should OpenClaw show to end users versus keep in logs, status metadata, or operator-only diagnostics?
rationale: The code already carries token, model, route, and session facts, but exposing raw session/channel identifiers and exact counts changes privacy, support, and channel UX behavior, so automation should not choose that policy alone.

options.title: Show Redacted Diagnostics
options.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted session/channel label while keeping raw identifiers in logs or metadata.

options.title: Keep Details Operator-Only
options.body: Keep chat copy generic and document how operators inspect logs/status metadata for exact context-pressure facts.

options.title: Defer To Broader Visibility Work
options.body: Keep this issue open until a broader context-visibility design chooses shared UI, logs, and channel-message behavior together.

recommendation.title: Show Redacted Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted session/channel label while keeping raw identifiers in logs or metadata.
